records.title: Notice of Motion - Improving Shared E-bike Safety in Lane Cove
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Flood and
seconded by Councillor Southwood that Council:
1. notes that:
a) shared e-bikes are an important part of the
transport mix and can provide our community with
an affordable and sustainable transport option,
b) residents have raised significant safety concerns
particularly relating to poorly parked or dumped
shared e-bikes.
2. acknowledges that staff are working with Lime on an
incremental roll out to undertake work on setting clear
standards for shared e-bike operators in our Local
Government Area (LGA) and further notes that this was
only made possible this year after the NSW Government
introduced regulations that have now been gazette that
impose minimum standards on shared bike operators
and gives councils some enforcement power in this
space.
3. investigates options for the Lane Cove LGA to create
additional dedicated marked parking zones (including
but not limited to no stopping zones for cars, or by
reallocating parking spaces as a last resort) in popular
areas, with input from relevant advisory committees,
including:
a) local smaller shopping/café precincts,
b) popular parks and sporting locations such as
Blackman, Galuwa etc,
c) residential pockets where trip data reveals a high
concentration of use.
4. undertakes a public education blitz to inform residents of
the new regulations and how to report inappropriately
parked bikes. Draw residents' attention to the parking
standard requirements in the new regulations and in
particular the requirement that a shared bike obstructing
a footpath or access point must be removed by the
operator within 3 hours – with fines for non-compliance;
and include designated link on Council’s Online Services
page to allow residents to report bikes that have not
been collected within the required time frame after report
to the relevant operator.
5. provides a report back to Council on how council is
working with the operators to monitor compliance and
how many breaches have been reported and enforced.
6. once the incremental rollout (trial period), referred to in 2
above, ends for Lime Bikes, seeks feedback from
residents and relevant advisory committees including the
Bike Committee, Sustainability Advisory Committee and
the Access and Age-Friendly Committee, to understand:
a) what worked well,
b) what could be improved,
c) are there hotspots or particular problem areas in the
LGA that need a greater enforcement focus.
7. provides to Councillors advice as to the liability of
Council, operators and/or bike users for damage, death
or injury arising from the use of shared e-bikes in the
Lane Cove LGA during the trial period
8. staff are to apply for the NSW Government "Sharing
Scheme Grant Program", which is a $6.6 million funding
initiative designed to help local councils manage shared
e-bikes (like Lime bikes) and reduce footpath clutter.
Under this program, Lane Cove Council may be eligible
for a grant of up to $200,000. This grant funding purpose
is for councils to:
a) build and mark dedicated e-bike parking bays and
kerbside spaces,
b) clear improperly dumped or clustered bikes from
pedestrian pathways,.
c) support local infrastructure adjustments tied to new
statewide micromobility regulations.

records.title: Mayoral Minute - Waste Infrastructure Planning
records.resolution:

Council:

Energy and for the Environment, the Minister for
Planning and Public Spaces, and the Minister for Crown
Lands, requesting that the NSW Government:
a) urgently develop a 20-year NSW Waste and
Circularity Infrastructure Roadmap,
b) reform Planning Pathways by:
i. amending the Transport and Infrastructure
State Environmental Planning Policy to include
waste infrastructure as permissible
development for public authorities or other

government, industry and relevant stakeholders to
develop the Roadmap and associated planning reforms,
recognising that councils are essential partners in the
planning and delivery of an integrated waste and circular
economy system.

planning through Resilient Sydney and the metropolitan
Regional Organisations of Councils.

records.title: Notice of Motion - Fur-Free Lane Cove
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Flood and
seconded by Councillor Greenwell that Council:
1. prohibit the sale of animal fur products on Public Council
land and at Council-owned or managed markets
(including third-party markets run on council land such
as the Makers Markets and Lane Cove Rotary Fair),
events, and community spaces.
2. for the purposes of this motion, ‘fur’ is defined in
accordance with the Fur Free Alliance definition as: any
animal skin or part thereof with hair or fur fibres
attached, either in its raw or processed state, or the pelt
of any animal killed for its fur. ‘Animal’ includes but is not
limited to, mink, fox, rabbit, karakul lamb and raccoon
dog. ‘Fur’ does not include:
a) skins that are, or are to be, converted into leather,
or from which the hair, fleece or fur fibres have
been completely removed;
b) materials clipped, shorn or combed from animals,
including fleece, sheepskin and shearling;
c) leather or hair attached to skin that is typically used
as leather, such as cowhide with hair attached;
d) synthetic materials intended to look like fur.
3. provide additional exemptions for:
a) taxidermy specimens (whole preserved animals or
skins prepared for educational, cultural, or display
purposes),
b) works of art where animal materials are used,
c) second-hand fur,
d) fur used and sold as part of the practice of
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural
heritage.
2. update relevant guidelines, including:
a) Market stall holder rules,
b) Event hire conditions,
c) Compliance checklists.
3. implement an education-first approach to enforcement
via existing compliance officers/rangers already in
attendance at market events.
4. add guidance on identifying real vs faux fur so both
stallholders and council officers are fully informed.
5. publish information on council’s website to provide
ethical options for the disposal of fur products (such as
the information provided by Liverpool Council).
6. write to the following requesting broader action:
a) NSW Minister for Fair Trading (state-wide retail
ban),
b) Federal Minister for Home Affairs & Minister for
Trade (import ban).

records.title: Notice of Motion - Growing Sporting Capacity without losing Green Space
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Bryla and
seconded by Councillor Kennedy that Council:
1. undertake a review of national and international best-
practice approaches to the planning and delivery of
sporting and recreational facilities that increase sporting
participation while protecting and enhancing urban tree
canopy, biodiversity, permeable landscapes and publicly
accessible open space. The review should consider
approaches that respond to:
a) increasing urban density and population growth;
b) the declining availability of traditional sporting
facilities;
c) climate change impacts, including extreme heat,
wet weather events and other conditions that
reduce the usability of outdoor sporting facilities;
and
d) emerging models of indoor, multi-purpose, shared
use and vertically integrated sporting infrastructure
(including sporting fields).
2. write to the NSW Minister for Education and Early
Learning and Deputy Premier, and the local school
Parents and Friends Associations, seeking support for
discussions between Lane Cove Council and local public
schools regarding community access to school sporting
facilities outside school operating hours, including:
a) the netball courts at Lane Cove Public School,
b) the grass sporting field at Greenwich Public School,
c) the basketball courts and open playing fields at
Lane Cove West Public School.
3. write to Sydney Catholic Schools seeking to commence
discussions regarding community access to sporting
facilities at St Michael's Catholic Primary School outside
school operating hours, including:
a) the netball court,
b) the indoor basketball court.
4. write to the Principal of St Ignatius’ College to
commence discussions regarding opportunities for
community access to the College's outdoor sporting
fields and other relevant sporting infrastructure.
5. investigate opportunities to support the growth and
provision of sporting facilities across Lane Cove through
planning mechanisms, including:
a) amendments to the Lane Cove Development
Control Plan, to encourage the provision of
sporting and recreation facilities in developments
where appropriate;
b) identifying opportunities for the delivery of indoor,
outdoor and innovative sporting infrastructure as
part of suitable major development sites including;
i. rooftop recreation space,
ii. sporting facilities above transport
infrastructure,
iii. integrated recreation facilities within schools,
iv. indoor sports hubs,
v. vertically integrated sporting infrastructure.
c) encouraging the delivery of sporting infrastructure
through Planning Agreements (PAs);
d) investigate potential amendments to the Lane Cove
Local Environmental Plan to incentivise the
provision of indoor sporting and recreational
facilities including consideration of "opportunity floor
space" or other bonus floor space provisions, where
appropriate.
6. prepare a report to Council outlining opportunities for
Lane Cove Council to:
a) advocate to the NSW Government, and Local
Government NSW (LGNSW), for a co-ordinated
regional approach to sporting facility provision that
moves beyond traditional LGA-based supply
models, while ensuring that any future initiatives to
increase sporting capacity seek, wherever
practicable, to avoid the net loss of publicly
accessible open green space and mature tree
canopy,
b) table to the Northern Sydney Regional Organisation
of Councils (NSROC) for their consideration,
b) identify innovative and collaborative regional
opportunities to address the growing shortage of
sporting and recreational facilities across the North
Shore, having regard to the matters outlined in
Items 1 and 5,
c) position the report as an advocacy document to
inform engagement with current and potential the
Members of Parliament representing Lane Cove in
the lead-up to the next State and Federal Elections,
with the aim of securing funding and policy support
for additional sporting and recreation infrastructure.

records.title: Notice of Motion - Development of a Draft Synthetic Turf in Public Spaces Policy and Investigation into synthetic turf guidelines for new dwellings
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Flood and
seconded by Councillor Southwood that Council:
1. subject to available funding, will use its best endeavours
to carry out works required to improve
the standard of playing surfaces of all its sports fields
to address the need for increased capacity and will work
with other Councils in NSROC to explore joint initiatives
to increase sports field capacity across the region.
2. confirms that there is no intention to remove the existing
synthetic turf on the sports fields at Blackman Park.
3. develops a draft Synthetic Turf in Public Spaces Policy
which incorporates the following key principles:
a) Council to prioritise the use of best practice and
sustainable natural turf solutions or other organic
solutions within public open space,
b) while there is a preference for best practice natural
turf, synthetic turf may be considered having regard
to the intended purpose of the public open space.
c) significant public work projects, which propose the
use of synthetic turf (including renewing synthetic
surfaces) are to come to the elected council for
decision,
d) a decision of Council will not be required to approve
use of synthetic turf on small areas that are critical
to the ongoing purpose of the open space, such
decisions to be reported to Councillors via the
Council Snapshot,
e) where synthetic turf has been selected to be used
for a capital works project, the project must be
developed and assessed against International best
practice standards for the use of synthetic surfaces
and in accordance with the NSW Government's
guidelines and recommendations for Councils
regarding synthetic turf (Division 5.1 Assessments –
Addendum for Synthetic Sports Fields May 2025),
f) where synthetic turf is to be used, the community
will be consulted on the proposed measures that
are being incorporated into the project to minimise
environmental and public health risk before the
approval of the project and subsequent
commencement
g) where synthetic turf is removed, best endeavours
are to be made to ensure that the material is
disposed of in an ethical and sustainable manner
4. will consult with and seek input from the community and
from relevant advisory committees, including the Sports
Clubs Advisory Committee, the Companion Animal
Committee, Access and Inclusion Committee, the
Bushland Management Advisory Committee, Youth
Advisory Group and the Sustainability Advisory
Committee.
5. in developing the draft policy, staff will have regard to
government publications and policies and evidence-
based research that address aspects of synthetic turf,
including but not limited to:
 loss of soil function, permeability and biodiversity
 elevated surface temperatures and increased urban
heat
 release of chemicals (Including PFAS) and
microplastics
 bushfire risk
 bacterial infections
 disposal and recycling at end of life.
6. will receive at a future council meeting a report on the
draft policy, and any approved draft will be subject to an
extended period of community consultation.
7. will simultaneously with the development of the Synthetic
Turf in Public Spaces Policy Council:
a) prepare guidance material for the community on
environmentally sustainable landscape alternatives
to synthetic turf available for private property,
including native planting, permeable surfaces, and
biodiverse gardens and
b) investigate whether development controls can be
incorporated into the Lane Cove Development
Control Plan to prevent the use of synthetic turf in
new private developments and report back to
Council on the outcomes of this investigation.

and Demand for Sports Facilities in the NSROC Region
as the most current regional evidence base for
organised sports facility demand across Northern
Sydney.
5. notes NSROC’s published findings that the region
requires increased sports facility capacity of
approximately:

 49% by 2036 (equivalent to 222 hectares),

participation demand.

c) principles for shared use, multi-code use and
equitable access
d) casual and community-use guidelines to protect
informal recreation
e) minimum utilisation expectations for allocated fields
f) maintenance, restoration and user responsibility
agreements
g) protocols for managing overuse, wet weather
closures and field carrying capacity
h) a dispute resolution and review process for
allocation decisions; and
i) annual reporting to Council on allocation outcomes,
utilisation, unmet demand and emerging pressures.
7. requests that the report also identify any gaps in
Council’s current policies, procedures or delegations
relating to the allocation and management of sporting
fields, including where clearer Council-adopted policy

records.title: Notice of Motion - Installation of Solar Panels on Galuwa Recreation Centre for maximising clean energy generation
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Bryla and
seconded by Councillor Kennedy that Council:
1. undertakes a Study to assess the viability of installing a
large-scale solar PV system, with optional battery
storage, maximising the roof capacity at the Galuwa
Sport and Recreation building, for the purpose of
generating and exporting electricity to the community or
other council facilities to provide a cost-effective solution
to support our local government area towards a
renewable energy future;
2. as part of the Study, prepares a report that includes (but
is not limited to):
a) a technical assessment of available roof space and
solar generation capacity;
b) an evaluation of implementation and operational
models that maximise environmental and
community benefit while minimising cost and risk to
Council, for example;
• Grid-connected microgrids;
• Stand-Alone Power Systems (SAPS);
• Community battery, Virtual Energy Networks;
• Community energy investment options; or
• energy supply for community buildings (such
as the Lane Cove Aquatic Centre);
c) an outline of (additional) battery storage benefits
and opportunities.
d) estimated capital costs, potential partnership
models (including third-party funding
arrangements),and projected payback periods;
e) opportunities to access state and federal grants, or
other funding streams;
f) analysis of local energy system benefits such as
grid support, demand reduction, and increased local
energy resilience;
g) opportunities to increase access to affordable
renewable energy for renters and those in
apartments;
3. writes to our Federal and State Members of Parliament
requesting financial support for the project; and
4 includes funding for the consultant work to undertake
this study for consideration to be included in the
2026/2027 budget, with work to commence in July 2026.
The consultant study is to be reported to Council in
February 2027 to enable consideration in the preparation
of the 2027/28 budget if the project is to proceed.

records.title: Notice of Motion - Planning for Water Sensitive Urban Design Principles and Greater Water Reuse to be implemented in Water Catchment Areas.
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Bryla and
seconded by Councillor Kennedy that Council:
1. invite a member from the Sydney Water Business
Development team to present to key council staff and
Councillors on the work they are undertaking,
2. provide a report to Council on resourcing and funds
required to implement the actions below:
a) Engage an external consultant to produce Water
Catchment Plans for Stringybark Creek and Burns
Bay Reserve that:
i) Outline targets to achieve water management
targets typically covering:
 Water quality/pollution reduction targets
 Runoff volume to protect local waterways
from erosion and degradation
 Urban/Waterway Outcome targets in terms
of biodiversity and urban cooling
ii) Provide a timeline to achieve these targets,
iii) Describe the methods to achieve the targets,
3. organise a meeting with the broader stakeholders who
may assist with grant funding and knowledge sharing for
Item 2. For example:
a) Representatives from adjoining
catchment areas including Parramatta
River catchment group and Lane Cove
River councils,
b) Representative from Department of Climate
Change, Energy and Environment and Water
(DCCEEW) NSW who are working on an
integrated water management framework, a
recycled water road map and Water Sensitive
Urban Design Policy,
c) Sydney Water and other agencies,
4. instigate a new communication engagement strategy
with workshops and campaigns:
a) to raise community awareness on how we can keep
our waterways clean, as well as promote rebates
Council offers for rainwater capture,
b) to raise awareness about the benefits of WSUD
among residents and businesses,
c) to encourage community participation in water-
sensitive initiatives, including optimising on-lot
stormwater retention infrastructure already in
place,
5. ensure the communication engagement strategies
also target residences and businesses in the related
two catchment areas of this motion; and
6. investigate how the current On The Verge program
could be expanded to include bioswales for verges
that are on contour.

records.title: Notice of Motion - Origin Destination Study: Karilla Avenue Lane Cove North
records.resolution:
RESOLVED on the motion moved by Councillor Flood and
seconded by Councillor Bryla that Council:
1. Consider the inclusion in the Delivery Program and
Operational Plan and Budget for 2025/2026 the
undertaking of an Origin-Destination study for cars using
Karilla Avenue to help evaluate whether the traffic
calming measures have reduced the volume of cars
using the two-way rat run,
2. Undertake the Origin-Destination study within 12 months
of the Karilla Avenue traffic calming measures being
installed. The study should assess rat-running (based on
the accepted Transport for NSW definition of rat-running)
during the recognised peak travel times and it shall not
be done during school holidays. It should, as closely as
possible, mirror the study undertaken previously to
provide a good point of comparison,
3. Receive a report comparing the new Origin-Destination
study data to the baseline results from the 2015/2016
study. If the study does not show a significant reduction
in rat-running, the report should outline additional
measures available to address specific concerns with
the Karilla Avenue rat-run.
